title: One manual, two chunking strategies: boundaries decide recall

events.label: Document ready
events.detail: A 62-page product manual: 12 chapters, 86 sections, 11 tables. Chunking happens before indexing — if this step goes wrong, everything after is wasted.

events.label: Into fixed chunking
events.detail: Strategy: a 512-token sliding window with 64-token overlap. Simplest to build; blind to document structure.

events.label: Produces 1070 chunks
events.detail: Tables cut in half; a section's opening squeezed into the previous section's tail. Overlap softens but does not solve it: of 1070 chunks, many are semantically incomplete fragments.

events.label: Indexed (1070 chunks)
events.detail: The more fragments, the heavier the noise dilution at retrieval time — relevant chunks get pushed around by irrelevant fragments.

events.label: Into structural chunking
events.detail: Strategy: split at heading levels and section boundaries; keep tables and code blocks whole; subdivide only overlong blocks.

events.label: Produces 320 chunks
events.detail: 1070 vs 320: fewer chunks, each semantically complete — the 'Return Policy' section lives entirely inside one chunk.

events.label: Indexed (320 chunks)
events.detail: Each chunk carries metadata: chapter number, heading path, update date — traveling with the chunk, so a hit can state its provenance.

events.label: Ask the question
events.detail: "Do I pay return shipping?" — the answer is one sentence inside the 'Return Policy' section.

events.label: Search the fixed-chunk store
events.detail: Bad luck: the answer sentence straddles the boundary of chunks 441/442 — 'shipping is paid by the buyer' sits in the tail of chunk 441.

events.label: Fixed-chunking recall
events.detail: Chunk 441 carries half the answer, semantically crippled, ranked third; chunk 442 with the other half scores lower and misses the top-3 — the answer was cut at the boundary, half of it lost.

events.label: Search the structural-chunk store
events.detail: Same question, different store — a controlled experiment.

events.label: Structural chunking hits
events.detail: The whole 'Return Policy' section hits at rank two, shipping rule intact inside the chunk — the answer is in the recalled chunk, and the model gets complete evidence.

events.label: Conclusion
events.detail: Chunk boundaries directly decide whether 'the answer is inside the recalled chunk'. Chunking is the first quality gate of RAG — cheaper than switching models, more effective than tuning parameters.
